s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with seizures, hemiparesis, and developmental delays
salient_findings: Upper motor neuron pattern of weakness
Focal abnormal brain activity on EEG
key_facts: Age of seizure onset: 3 months
Seizures have increased in frequency despite antiepileptic therapy
Delayed motor and cognitive milestones
Gradual behavioral changes, including disturbed sleep and irritability
No family history of neurological disorders
No reported perinatal complications or trauma
Normal routine laboratory studies, including metabolic and infectious panels
EEG shows focal abnormal brain activity
MRI demonstrates cerebral hemisphere atrophy and ex vacuo dilatation of the lateral ventricle
Ipsilateral calvarial thickening and compensatory hyperpneumatization of the sphenoid bone and bilateral mastoid air cells
Cystic encephalomalacia and gliosis in the right fronto-parieto-temporal region

differentials: Congenital hemidysplasia with ichthyosiform erythroderma and limb defects

shortlist.label: Rasmussen's encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Focal seizures, hemiparesis, and progressive neurological decline

shortlist.label: Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Cerebral hemisphere atrophy, ex vacuo dilatation of the lateral ventricle, and calvarial thickening

shortlist.label: Hemimegalencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres and significant atrophy of one hemisphere

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Seizures, hemiparesis, and possible cerebral atrophy

shortlist.label: Focal cortical dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Focal seizures and abnormal brain activity on EEG

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of seizures, hemiparesis, and cognitive impairment, along with the imaging findings of cerebral hemisphere atrophy, ex vacuo dilatation of the lateral ventricle, and ipsilateral calvarial thickening, are consistent with Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome, which is characterized by cerebral hemiatrophy and associated with seizures, hemiparesis, and intellectual disability.

rejected.label: Rasmussen's encephalitis
rejected.why: Rasmussen's encephalitis typically presents with more rapid progression of symptoms and often involves more widespread inflammation and tissue loss, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Hemimegalencephaly
rejected.why: Hemimegalencephaly is characterized by an overgrowth of one cerebral hemisphere, which is not consistent with the atrophy seen in this patient's imaging studies.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: Sturge-Weber syndrome typically involves a port-wine stain and leptomeningeal angiomatosis, which are not mentioned in this case.

rejected.label: Focal cortical dysplasia
rejected.why: Focal cortical dysplasia can cause seizures and may be associated with some imaging abnormalities, but it does not typically result in the widespread cerebral atrophy and hemispheric asymmetry seen in this patient.
